criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.description: Solution architecture, integrations with existing systems, scalability, performance and overall technical fit.

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.description: Timeline realism, milestones, staffing and team structure, delivery methodology and risk management plan.

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.description: Pricing clarity, total cost of ownership, stated assumptions, payment terms and value for money.

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.description: Security controls, certifications (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2), data privacy, auditability and regulatory compliance.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.description: Support model and SLAs, relevant similar projects, client references and track record.

formulas.benchmark: max score per criterion across suppliers
formulas.relative_pct: supplier score / benchmark * 100 (0 if benchmark is 0)

criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.justification: Apex provides a comprehensive cloud-native microservices architecture on Kubernetes with strong integration approaches (Kafka, 42 pre-built connectors including SAP S/4HANA and MultiSpeak MDM), automated data migration with reconciliation, and verified performance capabilities.
criteria.evidence: The platform uses a microservices architecture deployed on Kubernetes across two cloud availability zones in an Indian region, with active-active failover and a recovery point objective (RPO) of 5 minutes and recovery time objective (RTO) of 30 minutes.

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.justification: The implementation plan is detailed with a 40-week timeline, clear phases, specific milestones, rigorous data migration mock rehearsals, change management strategy, and an explicit risk register with assigned mitigations.
criteria.evidence: Delivery follows a phased hybrid approach: design waterfall for regulated billing rules, then agile two-week sprints for portal and integrations. Each phase ends with a documented exit review attended by the Board's PMO.

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.justification: Commercials feature a fixed-price implementation of INR 6.80 Cr and explicit yearly platform subscriptions totaling INR 14.21 Cr for 3 years (excluding GST). Payment terms are milestone-linked, and transparent rate cards are provided.
criteria.evidence: Total 3-year cost: INR 14.21 Cr (fixed price implementation), excludes GST

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.justification: The proposal demonstrates exceptional security and compliance controls, holding ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II certifications, bi-annual VAPT, AES-256 encryption, 24x7 SIEM monitoring, and strict DPDP Act alignment.
criteria.evidence: We hold ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II attestations, and our platform has been independently penetration tested every six months since 2021.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: Apex provides 24x7 support models with clearly defined SLAs, robust experienced team profiles, and strong reference cases from similar water and electricity utility billing implementations.
criteria.evidence: Apex has completed 6 utility billing implementations in the last 8 years, including two water utilities. Our utilities practice has 85 staff and a retention rate of 91 percent over the last three years.

risks: Apex acknowledges they are the highest-priced proposal in the expected market range, requiring a premium for dual-zone hosting and intensive monitoring.
Dependencies on the Board providing SAP and MDM test environments by week 9, which carries a medium risk of delay mitigated by virtual simulators and buffer time.
suppliers.overall_summary: Apex Systems presents a highly thorough, mature, and technically sound proposal for the Meridian Regional Water Board's platform modernisation. They demonstrate deep utility sector experience, robust architecture, detailed implementation and migration plans, and exemplary security compliance, justified by a higher-end fixed commercial price.
suppliers.rank_reason: Highest PPI after applying the tie-break order.

criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.justification: The technical architecture is thoroughly detailed, featuring a configurable utility billing product (NexaBill) on managed Kubernetes in India with a hot standby site. It addresses integrations with SAP S/4HANA and AMI MDM using REST APIs and message queues, scaling for 1.5 million connections.
criteria.evidence: We will implement our configurable utility billing product, NexaBill, on a managed cloud platform hosted in India, with a hot standby site. The platform exposes REST APIs and uses a message queue for asynchronous integration

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.justification: The implementation plan outlines a realistic 32-week timeline divided into five gated phases with clear entry and exit criteria. It includes a strong team structure, named key personnel, a detailed data migration and testing strategy, and an explicit risk management plan.
criteria.evidence: Our proposal is built around a proven delivery method, a realistic 32-week plan and a support model designed for 24x7 utility operations.

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.justification: Commercial pricing is clearly structured as a fixed-price implementation of INR 4.90 Cr and a total 3-year cost of INR 10.40 Cr, broken down by gates and annual subscription/hosting. Assumptions, payment terms, and out-of-scope change request day rates are explicitly stated.
criteria.evidence: Total 3-year cost: INR 10.40 Cr (fixed-price implementation), excludes GST

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.justification: The proposal includes robust security controls such as ISO 27001 certification, SOC 2 Type I completion (Type II in progress), AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, MFA, role-based access control, annual VAPT, and compliance with the DPDP Act with India-only data residency.
criteria.evidence: ISO 27001 certified (2023); SOC 2 Type I completed, Type II audit in progress.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: NexaWorks provides a dedicated 24x7 utility service desk with clear SLAs (15-minute P1 response, 4-hour resolution, 99.9% availability with service credits). They demonstrate strong relevant experience with 9 utility implementations in 7 years and provide fictional reference clients.
criteria.evidence: Our support model is a dedicated 24x7 utility service desk with a named account manager and customer success lead. SLA: Priority 1 response 15 minutes, resolution 4 hours

risks: Dependency on the Board providing SAP and MDM test environments by week 9, which could trigger mock endpoint usage and integration risks.
Potential for staff adoption challenges across the 11 zone offices, mitigated by a change champion network and floor-walkers.
SOC 2 Type II audit is still in progress (expected to complete in Q2 2027), meaning only Type I is currently completed.
suppliers.overall_summary: NexaWorks presents a comprehensive, structured, and technically sound proposal for the Meridian Regional Water Board's billing modernization. The response is notable for its clear five-gate delivery methodology, robust architecture around the NexaBill product, transparent fixed-price commercial model, solid security and compliance framework (ISO 27001, DPDP Act), and a well-defined 24x7 support model backed by relevant utility experience.
suppliers.rank_reason: Below Apex Systems: higher PPI (100.00 vs 92.00).

criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.justification: Orbit proposes its mature UtilityOne billing and customer engagement suite, hosted in a cloud region in India. However, details regarding system integrations (such as SAP S/4HANA and MDM) are deferred entirely to the discovery phase, with scalability and performance targets also left to be agreed later.
criteria.evidence: Integration approach: integrations with SAP and the meter data management system will be determined during the discovery phase once we understand the Board's landscape.

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.justification: The proposal outlines a structured 36-week methodology (OrbitWay) broken down into four distinct phases: discovery (8 weeks), configuration (16 weeks), testing (8 weeks), and deployment (4 weeks). However, the team size and detailed project milestones are left to be confirmed after discovery.
criteria.evidence: Team: an engagement partner, a project manager and a team of consultants whose size will be confirmed after discovery. Detailed milestones will be agreed after discovery.

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.justification: The total estimated 3-year cost is provided as INR 10.85 Cr, broken down into implementation services, licenses, and training. However, the implementation pricing is entirely on a time-and-materials basis (not fixed or capped) and is subject to change based on discovery findings.
criteria.evidence: Note that the total above is an estimate and not a fixed or capped price.

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.justification: Orbit Digital is ISO 27001 certified and complies with Indian data protection regulations. The solution supports role-based access control, data encryption in transit and at rest, audit logging, and annual penetration testing, though disaster recovery objectives are to be agreed in design.
criteria.evidence: Orbit Digital is ISO 27001 certified. UtilityOne supports role-based access control, encryption of data in transit and at rest, and audit logging.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: Orbit demonstrates strong experience in the utilities sector with 18 years in business, 22 completed billing implementations, 14 utility clients, and 5 reference clients who agreed to be contacted. They also provide a 24x7 Bengaluru service centre for critical incidents with a 1-hour P1 response time.
criteria.evidence: Experience: 18 years in utilities, 14 utility clients and 22 completed billing implementations, including water, electricity and gas utilities.

risks: Implementation pricing is entirely time-and-materials and not fixed/capped, meaning total costs could escalate significantly after discovery.
Integration scope with SAP S/4HANA and Meter Data Management (MDM) is completely undefined and subject to discovery, introducing delivery and cost uncertainty.
Team size, detailed milestones, data migration approach, and test data specifics are all deferred until after contract award/discovery.
suppliers.overall_summary: Orbit Digital presents a comprehensive and mature utility billing suite (UtilityOne) backed by extensive industry experience (22 implementations across 14 utility clients) and solid security credentials like ISO 27001. Their proposed 36-week delivery methodology is clear, and they offer strong support terms with 24x7 critical incident coverage. However, the proposal carries notable commercial and technical risks because the implementation pricing is strictly time-and-materials, and critical elements such as integration scope, team size, data migration, and detailed milestones are entirely deferred to a post-award discovery phase.

criteria.name: Technical Capability
criteria.justification: BrightPath proposes its low-code QuickBill platform running on a single cloud server with daily backups. However, QuickBill was only released in 2024 and is currently used by just two small clients for subscription billing. Integration with the finance system relies on monthly file exports, and they admit they do not currently have performance test results for volumes similar to the Board's customer base.
criteria.evidence: QuickBill was first released in 2024 and is used by two small clients for subscription billing.

criteria.name: Implementation Plan
criteria.justification: The proposal includes a clear 16-week timeline broken down into stages (Setup, Customisation, Testing, Go-live) and uses an agile delivery methodology with weekly demos. The team structure is small (1 project lead and 4 developers). Risk management is weak, handled ad-hoc by the project lead, and data migration effort is unestimated because they haven't seen the Board's data structure.
criteria.evidence: Stage: Setup and configuration (Weeks 1-4), Customisation (5-11), Testing (12-14), Go-live (15-16).

criteria.name: Commercial Value
criteria.justification: Pricing is clearly itemized with a total 3-year cost of INR 6.04 Cr (Implementation/customisation at 2.40 Cr, QuickBill licence at 3.60 Cr, Training at 4 Lakhs). Payment terms are 50% on contract signature and 50% on go-live. However, prices are marked as indicative, hosting costs are excluded, and changes after contract are quoted separately.
criteria.evidence: Total 3-year cost: INR 6,04,00,000. Payment terms: 50 percent on contract signature and 50 percent on go-live.

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.justification: Security controls are basic, relying on usernames, passwords, and the cloud provider's standard firewall. They do not currently hold certifications like ISO 27001 or SOC 2, though ISO 27001 is 'planned' to begin next year. Formal SLAs and specific regulatory compliance details are weak or deferred.
criteria.evidence: User names and passwords; Cloud provider's standard firewall; ISO 27001 planned.

criteria.name: Support & Experience
criteria.justification: Support hours are limited to Monday through Friday, 9 am to 6 pm via email, with a 1-day response target and no formal SLA currently offered. BrightPath has delivered 3 web portals for retail and education clients, but explicitly notes this would be their first utility billing project.
criteria.evidence: Support is available Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm, by email. We aim to respond within one business day.

risks: BrightPath Tech is a young company founded in 2022 with only 28 employees, and QuickBill was only released in 2024 with experience limited to two small subscription billing clients.
No prior experience in the utility or water sector; this would be their first utility billing project.
Absence of performance test results for volumes matching the Board's customer base, relying on a single cloud server.
Integrations rely heavily on manual or scheduled file exports (e.g., monthly finance file exports) rather than real-time APIs.
Basic security controls with no current certifications (ISO 27001 is only planned for next year).
Limited support model (business hours only, email-based, 1-day response target, no formal SLA).
suppliers.overall_summary: BrightPath Tech presents an energetic, low-cost proposal centered around their low-code QuickBill platform with a rapid 16-week delivery timeline. While the commercial pricing is clear and the agile methodology is well-articulated, the proposal carries significant execution and operational risks. These include a complete lack of prior utility sector experience, unproven scalability for large customer volumes, basic security controls without current certifications, limited support hours without an SLA, and reliance on manual file exports for integrations.
